input.sha256_scope: No image input beyond a zero-filled shape. The concatenation cases are synthetic page dicts, which are the function's complete input; the merge cases are synthetic layout/span specs in the style of classic-v1-layout-assembly. The expected file is both the input record and the expected record.
input.provenance: Authored in tools/capture_multipage_oracle.py, importing the page-building constants and stubs from tools/capture_layout_assembly_oracle.py.

upstream.capture_method: Both functions were executed as unbound methods against a DummySelf, which neither touches. concatenate_markdown_pages ran over eight synthetic page lists covering every branch: the paragraph break, the ASCII inline join, a CJK character on each side, an empty continuing page, a single page, flag propagation across three pages, and the empty list. merge_text_across_page ran over four multipage block lists, each page built by the executed post-model chain (standardized_data, get_layout_parsing_objects, sort_layout_parsing_blocks, the order_index tail). Recorded per merge case: the block count per page before merging, and the surviving blocks with label, content, and group_id.
upstream.environment: python 3.12, paddlex 3.7.2, numpy 2.x, opencv-contrib-python 5.x (IO backend only)

limitations: The concatenation cases supply page dicts directly rather than running whole pages through _to_markdown first. That is deliberate: the function reads only page_continuation_flags and markdown_texts, so a synthetic pair is the complete input, and classic-v1-markdown-v2 already checks that this port produces those two values correctly.
cases_that_merged records which merge cases actually dropped a block, so a reimplementation that never merges cannot pass by reproducing only the no-merge case.

Neither function is reachable from a real multipage input in this port: PDF-001 has no approved renderer, so these are unit-level guarantees over the document assembly, not an end-to-end multipage claim.
